children: Australian travel booker WebBeds loses its bull at Macquarie amid worries over the potential effects of an audit by Spanish tax authorities. Lowering their recommendation to "neutral" from "outperform," an analyst at the investment bank tells clients in a note that WebBeds is performing well operationally but that the implications of the continuing audit are unclear. WebBeds has recognized a fiscal first-half charge of 50 million Australian dollars but the analyst points out that any effect on future earnings is unclear. Macquarie lowers its target price on the stock 38%, to A$2.64. Shares are at A$2.60 ahead of the open. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
